💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, samsung is preparing its next major revision for Galaxy phones, One UI 9.5, and upcoming details have been coming to light.
  • One UI 9.5 will still be based on Android 17, but it’s set to be packed with various changes based on recent leaks.
  • Sources indicate that “Galaxy Claw” is supposedly Samsung’s new “personal agent,” able to leverage apps on your device including your notifications, Contacts, Gmail, Messages, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, samsung is preparing its next major revision for Galaxy phones, One UI 9.5, and upcoming details have been coming to light. Here’s an overview of a lot of One UI 9.5 updates that have leaked so far.

One UI 9.5 will still be based on Android 17, but it’s set to be packed with various changes based on recent leaks. In particular, it seems like Samsung has a ton of latest AI features in store.

Sources indicate that “Galaxy Claw” is supposedly Samsung’s new “personal agent,” able to leverage apps on your device including your notifications, Contacts, Gmail, Messages, and more. Specifically, Android Authority reports it will be able to use Calendar, Contacts, Gallery, Gmail, Messages, Notifications, Perplexity, Phone, and Voice Recorder, with the agent able to set up scheduled tasks. It does sound like this will be a paid feature, though, with Samsung’s new $4.99/month AI Premium plan. There would also be a new dashboard for showing AI usage.

There’s also a new Memory feature in Bixby that would let the assistant reference past details from conversations or commands.

Daily Brief, sharing its name with Google’s canceled Pixel feature, would be able to summarize notifications from various apps, grouping cards into “Finance and payments,” “Bookings and appointments,” and “Work email,” though that list seems incomplete.

It’s not all about AI. It also looks like Samsung’s Expert RAW camera experience is being improved with better labels, customizable buttons, a screen lock option, burst mode support, and more. It even seems like there’s video support coming.

Other new features that have leaked include:.

Sources indicate that one UI 9.5 will almost certainly be launching on next year’s Galaxy S27 series before expanding to more devices later on, as has been the case for the past several updates. A beta program will likely be available on Galaxy S26 series soon – the One UI 8.5 beta program opened up in early December 2025.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’re only a couple of months away from our next Galaxy Unpacked, and while the expanded Galaxy S27 series is practically guaranteed to show up, the real fun tends to lie in whatever other gadgets show up alongside Samsung’s next flagship smartphone release.
  • Samsung hasn’t produced over-ear headphones in about a decade — under its own name, at least — but it looks like that’s about to change.
  • Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, Galaxy Studio will include ANC, complete with a dedicated button to toggle the setting between its usual modes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’re only a couple of months away from our next Galaxy Unpacked, and while the expanded Galaxy S27 series is practically guaranteed to show up, the real fun tends to lie in whatever other gadgets show up alongside Samsung’s next flagship smartphone release. Based on some fresh leaks, it’s sure looking like the next mobile accessory on the manufacturer’s docket is a return to over-ear wireless headphones, and so far, they’re sounding pretty promising.

Samsung hasn’t produced over-ear headphones in about a decade — under its own name, at least — but it looks like that’s about to change. We hadn’t heard much in the way of details on the manufacturer’s next audio release, rumored to be named ‘Galaxy Studio,’ but a fresh leak courtesy of SamMobile is finally changing that. We’ll have to keep waiting for full renders, but these leaked graphics are giving us a general idea of what they might look like, plus a couple of key features.

Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, Galaxy Studio will include ANC, complete with a dedicated button to toggle the setting between its usual modes. Volume controls also could come in the shape of physical buttons, but playback controls appear to be relegated to a touch-sensitive area on its earpads, something that’s become relatively standard among the flagship headphone competition. SamMobile also reports it’ll come in “at least” black and red colorways, while a leak from earlier this month suggested rotational earcups.

It has been revealed that again, I don’t want to read too much into these leaked graphics, as it’s always possible the final release has a handful of changes. Based on these images, though, I’m pleasantly surprised to see Samsung avoiding an attempt at copying Apple’s AirPods Max design. The larger cups, combined with their ability to twist and turn for easy storage, sounds much closer to most (but not all) of Sony’s over-ear efforts across the last decade or so, and when it comes to headphones, there are much, much worse choices you could look to for inspiration. If Samsung can hit the right price on these — or bundle them with one of their ever-more-expensive smartphones — they could be a real winner.

MagSafe Monday: MOFT’s Trackable Field Wallet holds eight cards, cash, and supports Find My

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the one thing Apple’s own MagSafe wallet does that a few third-party wallets have is Find My.
  • MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.
  • MOFT has been making the origami-style folding wallet for many years, and this model works like any other Find My accessory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the one thing Apple’s own MagSafe wallet does that a few third-party wallets have is Find My. If you misplace your wallet, your iPhone tells you where it is. Most MagSafe wallets either skip tracking entirely or have a pocket for an AirTag, which adds thickness and it’s another thing to buy. The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet builds the tracker into the wallet itself, so it highlights up in the Find My app.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

MOFT has been making the origami-style folding wallet for many years, and this model works like any other Find My accessory. So that means you get left-behind alerts when you leave without it, and the ability to make it trackable through Apple’s network if it’s across town instead of under the couch. It also works with Google’s Find Hub on Android, which matters if you’ve got a mixed household of devices.

Industry observers note that the wallet is powered by a built-in battery rather than a watch-style battery, and MOFT states a charge lasts about six months. You charge it by placing the wallet on a Qi charger for about an hour and a half, which, in practice, means dropping it on a MagSafe dock twice a year. That’s a better setup than an AirTag in a wallet as well.

It has been revealed that the wallet holds up to eight cards, or closer to four to six if you also use the hidden compartment for cash. A pull tab in the wallet brings your everyday cards out in one motion, while your driver’s license and cash stay tucked inside of it. It’s made from MOFT’s vegan leather and at 14 mm thick, it’s slimmer than a traditional wallet but noticeably thicker than Apple’s card-only wallet, which is the price you are going to pay to hold up this much stuff.

Industry observers note that the stand is the usual MOFT origami fold-out, and it works in portrait and landscape for FaceTime or watching a video on the plane. You can buy it without the stand if you’d rather have the thinner version. It comes in Jet Black, Misty Cove, Terracotta, and Peony.

In a recent development, two things to know going in. There’s no RFID blocking in this version (MOFT has a non-Find My Snap Field Wallet if you want that). MOFT also warns that the magnets can affect magnetic-stripe cards, so avoid putting a hotel key in it.

In a recent development, I’ve spent the past month on a Pelican accessory beat, using wallets designed for outdoor use. The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet is the other end of that accessory spectrum: more cards, a stand, and Find My built in. If Find My is the reason you’ve stuck with Apple’s wallet, this is a really nice option that holds a bunch and is trackable.

The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet is available on Amazon and directly from MOFT.

Gemini rolling out 66 new regional voices on Android and iOS, including 10+ UK dialects

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, following a preview at Google I/O, Google is rolling out 66 new regional voices to the Gemini app on both Android and iOS today.
  • For people in the UK, the update brings over 10 distinct English voice options covering a wide range of regional cadences.
  • This might help reduce the problems that sometimes still occur when English accents, in particular, morph into a hybrid of Australian or even American that has been going on for a while with Gemini Live.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, following a preview at Google I/O, Google is rolling out 66 new regional voices to the Gemini app on both Android and iOS today. The expansion introduces tailored voice options across U.S. English, U.K. English, Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean.

For people in the UK, the update brings over 10 distinct English voice options covering a wide range of regional cadences. The lineup includes Geordie, Scouse, Brummie, Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish, Modern RP, and Multicultural London English (MLE).

This might help reduce the problems that sometimes still occur when English accents, in particular, morph into a hybrid of Australian or even American that has been going on for a while with Gemini Live. We have not yet been able to test to confirm this has been resolved with the patch. As someone with a regional English accent, this extra representation with Gemini voices is quite welcome.

According to Google, these voices are tuned for natural pronunciation, pitch, and everyday local rhythm rather than exaggerated stereotypes. Because the focus is on cadence over slang, Gemini will sound like a local without filling its text responses with forced street slang. Once selected, your chosen voice carries across the entire app, applying to both Gemini Live conversations and standard text-to-speech playback when tapping the “Listen” icon on chat responses.

You can preview and select the latest options today by tapping the three-dot menu inside Gemini Live, or by heading into the Gemini app settings and selecting “Gemini’s voice.” It’s worth noting that the voices aren’t explicitly labeled by city or region in the app menu, and Gemini isn’t programmed to self-identify which accent it is using if you ask it directly.

Instead, Google notes that locally rooted prompts about food, culture, or sport, such as asking for the best pub in Sheffield for a Sunday roast – my suggestion is not a pub; it’s Turnip & Thyme on Eccleshall Road, FWIW. Or another suggestion from big G is where to find proper ingredients for a traditional Scouse stew; the company claims these will naturally bring out the warmth and rhythm of the upcoming dialects.

I’d suggest trying to ask where to get the best pattie and chips in Hull or where to get the best pint in Leeds (it’s Whitelocks).

#1607. Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday: Which day should you shop for the best deals?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1162 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday: Which day should you shop for the best deals?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza.
  • Sources indicate that while major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on big-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices).
  • Sources indicate that if you're debating when you should start adding big-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza. The lines really began to blur when the world shut down in 2020, and brick-and-mortar stores hosted online sales in lieu of in-person Black Friday events. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them.

Sources indicate that while major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on big-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices). That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals.

Sources indicate that if you're debating when you should start adding big-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place. After years of covering both sales extensively, here's our expert analysis.

Way back in the age of MySpace and AIM — aka 2005 — the National Retail Federation debuted the term "Cyber Monday" after realizing that the Monday after Thanksgiving saw a flood of online sales. This was likely due to shoppers using their faster internet connections at work on Monday morning to snag deals, or at least that's what they credited it to. That, of course, and the fact that online retailers wanted some of that holiday shopping bread, too. Thus, two distinct deal-shopping days were born: Black Friday, for those who wanted to shop in stores the day after Thanksgiving, and Cyber Monday, for those who preferred shopping from the comfort of their desks.

Industry observers note that over 20 years later, there's little — if any — real difference between the two due to the alleged "death of retail." Everyone and everything is online, so why wouldn't Black Friday be? Based on our years of experience covering both, we can truly say neither is a "better" day to shop. It really comes down to what you're looking for and how much demand there is for it. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

If you see a solid deal, grab it, no matter which sale title it falls under. There's not a tremendous amount of distinction anymore in terms of discounts on particular products, as there was in previous years. However, there are still rules to follow in some product categories: TV deals tend to be more dramatic and widespread for Black Friday, with a higher likelihood of selling out before the clock even turns to Cyber Monday, while waiting for Cyber Monday to double-check that there's not a newly introduced, better laptop deal is often wise.

But with the blurred lines of Cyber Week, many of these deals will cross over. As noted at BlackFriday.com, "Some TV deals will feature flashy discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but they might not have the specs you're after.".

Recent findings suggest that TL;DR: The deals will be great for both shopping days, but it all depends on what you're looking for. If you see specs you like listed under a product at a price you like, grab it to be safe.

Black Friday proper falls on Nov. 27 in 2026, but it's honestly silly to even call it Black Friday at this point. It's no longer just on Friday — it's a month-long affair. You can shop deals at practically every retailer starting right after Halloween (before, even), with most labeling something an "early Black Friday deal" as early as November. Best Buy's official early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 6, while Target's began on Nov. 5. Amazon's actual Black Friday sale starts Nov. 19, but you can already find the "early Black Friday deal" tag on plenty of listings. In other words, if you want to get some early shopping done, have at it.

Once the clock strikes midnight on Friday, it's basically Cyber Monday (yes, even though it's actually Saturday). We don't make the rules. The deals won't change too much, but the search terms and official site banners will.

According to recent reports, officially, Cyber Monday is on Monday, Nov. 30 in 2026. Unofficially, it basically starts the second Black Friday ends, with retailers calling sales "Cyber Monday" deals as early as Saturday, Nov. 28. So basically, semantics — and it's easier to just think of the Cyber Week language as interchangeable.

Topics Black Friday Cyber Monday.

Black Friday will last most of November, but come Saturday, Nov. 28, it's Cyber Monday time. As we mentioned above, since Black Friday and Cyber Monday are basically one massive shopping holiday, you likely won't see that many changes in deals, just changes in the banners and advertising of them.

Cyber Monday sales will last from Saturday, Nov. 28 to midnight on Monday, Nov. 30. There's not a hard stop, as there's always deals that stay live for at least the day or two following, but the large bulk of the sale is over once Monday ends.

It has been revealed that as store policy, Target stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day, but are open for Black Friday beginning at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27.

Sources indicate that walmart will be open from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27. Walmart has confirmed that physical stores will be closed on Thanksgiving Day "so associates can spend the day with their families.".

All physical Best Buy locations will be closed on Thanksgiving. Doors will open at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27 for shoppers and close at 10 p.m.

All Kohl's stores are closed on Thanksgiving but are open for in-store shopping beginning at 5 a.m. local time on Nov. 27, per a press release.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) was finally released into the wild on Nov. 19, unveiling the beloved video game franchise's first title in 13 years. The highly anticipated game even inspired eager fans to take time off work in favor of immersing themselves in GTA 6, reveling in everything from crashing planes to home renovation in-game.

Industry observers note that yet while our virtual avatars engage in miscellaneous violent crimes, our physical bodies still require sustenance. Food delivery apps such as Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Grubhub have thus jumped on the GTA 6 hype, offering discount codes to those too locked in to their marathon gaming session to cook.

DoorDash's GTA 6 discounts are the most limited in terms of food options, offering $6 off Cheesecake Factory orders of $20 or more. Customers just need to enter the discount code CAKEGTA6 when placing their DoorDash order, with the offer only available on Nov. 19.

In a recent development, the company is also offering $15 off orders of $20 or more from Wendy's with codes given out on the Wendy's Twitch stream until 9 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PT (check the scrolling bar at the top of the screen). However, these DoorDash codes are limited to the first 100 customers, and only valid for 30 minutes after they're released.

Sources indicate that uber Eats' discount code ONAMISSION will save owners $10 off an order of $20 or more, and isn't restricted to a specific restaurant. Uber Eats has indicated this code is specifically for GTA 6's launch day, so if you're interested you should redeem it sooner rather than later.

Grubhub's discount code OUTOFOFFICE offered $10 off orders over $10, and was active from 9 a.m. ET / 6 a.m. PT on GTA 6 launch day. Unfortunately, it was limited to the first 1,000 customers, with some people reporting that they were unable to use the code within minutes of the promotion being posted. Less than an hour and a half later, Grubhub confirmed that its GTA 6-inspired discount code had been exhausted.

Food delivery apps have apparently received an influx of orders surrounding GTA 6's launch. The Latest York Times reports that DoorDash's energy drink sales spiked by over 20 percent on Wednesday, when many Grand Theft Auto fans stayed up for the game's midnight launch. DoorDash's Wednesday night sales were reportedly up by double digits in multiple U.S. states, while UberEats' overnight sales increased by 30 percent in Miami (the inspiration behind GTA 6's Vice City).

The next few days may be busy for food delivery workers, with gamers expected to spend hours exploring GTA 6. As such, remember to be patient and tip well. No doubt they'd rather be playing as well.

While it was obvious that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps would increase over time, their limited availability was a substantial part of the conversation around early reviews and online commentary in the first days after the device launched.

In a recent development, over 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo! That number DOUBLED in just over a week.I’m excited by how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can’t wait to see what they build next.

Joswiak’s upgrade came on the same day that Apple released iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, which addresses two other common complaints from early iPhone Duo reviews: the lack of Face ID, and the inability to automatically lock the device when closing it.

As 9to5Mac covered earlier today, the second developer beta of iOS 27.3 introduces a new unlock option that uses the outer display’s camera to recognize the user’s face, as well as a setting to automatically lock the device when folded shut.

The latter addresses a common complaint from users who found it strange that closing the phone didn’t automatically lock it, requiring them to press the side button instead.

Oppo is set to unveil its next mid-range phones in China next week, but the specs may have already leaked. According to reliable Weibo tipster Digital Chat Station, the Oppo Reno 17 series will consist of two models: the base Reno 17 and an upgraded Reno 17 Pro.

Interestingly, the cheaper of the two phones will apparently have the larger screen, coming in at 6.56 inches at a 1.5K resolution (the Reno 17 Pro's display, meanwhile, is a 6.32-inch 1.5K panel). On top of that, they claim the Reno 17 will be powered by the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 SoC – a mid-range, 8-core chipset already found in this year's Oppo Reno 16 as well as similarly priced competitors like the Honor 600 and Nothing Phone (4a) Pro.

According to recent reports, as for the cameras, the Reno 17 will reportedly have a 50MP front selfie camera and a three-sensor rear camera setup featuring a 50MP main shooter, 50MP ultra-wide, and 50MP 3.5x periscope telephoto lens. If the leak is indeed accurate, the lack of a significant chip upgrade this generation is a shame, but it seems buyers of this newer model can at least look forward to improved battery life.

Digital Chat Station claims the Reno 17 will have an 8,000mAh cell with support for speedy 80W charging, a major upgrade over the Reno 16's 6,000mAh battery that should be able to handle multiple days of use on a single charge more comfortably — though it's yet to be seen whether the UK and European models will have the same capacity as the Chinese model.

It has been revealed that aside from the difference in screen size, the Pro model will allegedly offer an upgraded 200MP main camera and a significantly more powerful MediaTek Dimensity 8550 Super processor. The battery of the Pro seems slightly smaller than that of the base model, coming at 7,200mAh with the same 80W fast charging.

Both the Reno 17 and Reno 17 Pro are remarked to have metal bodies and feature optical fingerprint sensors. There's no word on RAM, storage capacity, or color options yet. We'll be watching the Chinese release closely for more details.

Google Messages always has something going on, be it a UI patch or the addition of a latest feature - and the messaging service could be rolling out not one, but two handy tools soon.

First up, it appears that Google Messages is getting some voice note improvements, as spotted by Android Authority in one of its recent APK teardowns.

In a recent development, sick and tired of voice note playback stopping when you leave a chat? Google is fixing this.

Sources indicate that at the moment, you can listen to voice notes and audio files when you switch to a different app, but it stops when you leave a chat and return to the main conversation list. Although it's not live yet, Android Authority claims it managed to enable a feature, which it notes allows audio playback to continue even when exiting a chat. This finally deals with a huge pain point, allowing you to listen to a voice note from one person when replying to another in a separate conversation.

Sources indicate that this is the biggest upgrade when it comes to voice notes and audio files, but it's not the only one Google is working on. Additionally, the outlet spotted new playback control buttons in the notification center, including new pause, play, and forward icons supporting 5- to 30-second skip and rewind.

It has been revealed that as far as aesthetics go, Google is tipped to roll out small but noticeable changes for icons within chats. If the newly introduced features roll out, the voice note icon could change from its current wave-like symbol to a standard microphone, which makes more sense, though I can see it being mistaken for a speech-to-text function.

Industry observers note that when you have friends and family constantly on your case, organizing your conversations can make a huge difference, but Google Messages' six-pin limit just isn't enough to suffice for some customers. Thankfully, this could soon be a thing of the past.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Android Authority carried out another deep dive into Google Messages' latest beta, finding strings that point to the possibility of Google lifting its long-time pin restrictions as well as reviving its old chat pins layout.

In a recent development, depending on how many chats you pin, the layout will switch based on this number. If you pin six chats or fewer, your conversations will appear in the current tile-based design. If you pin more than six, your chats will automatically switch to the app's previous list-based layout, which allowed you to pin up to 20 different conversations - though we don't know if that number will be reinstated for this upgrade; the strings in Android Authority's findings don't clarify that.

As it is with every teardown, it's not guaranteed that the features in development will see the light of day. There's always the chance that Google could abandon the ideas altogether. That said, if the upgrades remain on Google's release calendar, there's no doubt they'd be welcomed quality-of-life upgrades for those who rely on Google Messages to stay connected.

Wars final verdict explained by Dominic West and Sienna Miller

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a full season of cutthroat legal proceedings, War's central divorce trial between actor Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) and tech mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) has reached its final verdict.
  • It has been revealed that that's because, after some eleventh-hour heroics from mole Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) and honeypot Flora Monroe (Rose Williams), Carla and Morgan reach their own settlement, independent of their lawyers and the judge.
  • Their decision stems from hearing Flora read Morgan's conciliatory letter to Carla, which St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a full season of cutthroat legal proceedings, War's central divorce trial between actor Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) and tech mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) has reached its final verdict. The winner? No one. But the loser? Also no one.

It has been revealed that that's because, after some eleventh-hour heroics from mole Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) and honeypot Flora Monroe (Rose Williams), Carla and Morgan reach their own settlement, independent of their lawyers and the judge. Following their decision, Carla will receive 50 percent of Zephyr's shares and monthly payments from Morgan until he retires. Carla and Morgan will share custody of Carla's son, Gabe (Aran Murphy). In short, it's basically what Carla had been asking for this whole time, and what the pair could have achieved without going to court.

Their decision stems from hearing Flora read Morgan's conciliatory letter to Carla, which St. John Smallwood (Pip Torrens) tried to dispose of, aloud in court. For Carla and Morgan, the letter is a reminder of the good in their relationship, something they sorely needed to recall after months of highly public mud-slinging.

"It tied itself up with humanity and kindness, and that was unexpected for me when I was reading it," Miller told Mashable in a junket interview alongside West. "I think the moral of that being that had these two people dropped their ego and their pride and nasty covetousness, if they'd let all of that go, they could have probably resolved this without the hideous experience of taking each other to court.".

"It felt like a spectacular waste of $10 million on lawyers' fees," West joked.

For series creator George Kay, there was never a version of War Season 1 where the court ruled in favor of one side or the other.

Sources indicate that "In the majority of these significant divorces, the real winners are the lawyers, and so we wanted to take that agency away from the justice system and put it back in the hands of [Carla and Morgan]," Kay told Mashable in a junket interview. "So, it was always going to be down to them to work it out, which is the big expensive irony of what they've been through.".

Sources indicate that by the end of Season 1, Carla and Morgan have found what seems to be an affectionate alliance. Even though Carla now has the Zephyr shares she asked for, she won't be using them against Morgan to trigger the sale to Michael Ancker (David Menkin), as Zephyr CEO Gillian Pope (Angel Coulby) wanted. Instead, Gillian is being ousted, as it turns out she leaked the security footage of Flora leaving Morgan's hotel room to the press.

In War's final scene between Carla and Morgan, the pair stand, at peace, on a Normandy beach by their cottage.

"I'll always love you," Morgan tells Carla.

Industry observers note that as it seems that the pair is about to go their separate ways, Carla calls Morgan back up to the cottage for a hot chocolate with Gabe. It's proof that their life as a pairing isn't over. It's just taken a different shape. And maybe thanks to that, both Carla and Morgan "won" in the trial after all.

Industry observers note that "The end of a divorce, it's not like someone's dead," West mentioned. "You either never speak to each other again, run screaming through the streets, or you realize actually why you love the person in the first place. I think that's what happens to Morgan in the end.".

"We described this divorce at the world's most expensive couples therapy, because it's only by going through everything that they've been through, hearing what the other one thinks via their lawyers, emotionally reengaging with everything they've had in their relationship, that by the end they realize what an amazing thing they have, and so we leave them okay," Kay said. "They're divorced, technically, but actually they're much better parents and they're much closer emotionally, and that was always a North Star for us.".

It has been revealed that the sweet ending for Morgan and Carla is at odds with the rest of War's bloodthirsty, win-at-any-cost tone. But for Kay, that was intentional.

It has been revealed that "We didn't want it to be bleak or dark," Kay remarked of the ending. "We wanted it to be redemptive.".

It has been revealed that google Maps wants to help you blueprint everything from small getaways to full holiday itineraries. The tech giant's latest Ask Maps update rolls out with a few vital changes.

Industry observers note that planning a big trip can be difficult, but Google's Ask Maps patch aims to make it easier. In a blog post, the manufacturer states owners rely on Ask Maps to plan road trips or a day out eating at various restaurants in their area. Google's AI will provide a "day-by-day schedule with insider tips and numbered map pins for each stop.".

Ask Maps operates similarly to Gemini's chats. Consumers can revisit previous chats with the AI by searching for an "itinerary badge." Each stop the AI selects for your trip includes traffic details, opening/closing times, and options to edit your schedule yourself. If you don't want something there, you can kick it. Users can also tell Ask Maps to add a "scenic stop" or something else you'd find more interesting.

After you set your trip, you can share your itinerary with others.

According to recent reports, elsewhere, Google says it's brought its agentic AI capabilities from Gemini into Maps. This lets people handle more complex tasks. Users can tell the AI to find a place for a specific appointment. It will reportedly display options that fit what you're looking for (nails, hair, dentist, time, etc.). These capabilities extend to users searching for restaurants at a specific time for a set number of people.

Google indicates these Ask Maps updates are rolling out today (No. 16) on Android and iOS. What's more, the company is bringing this feature to thirty additional countries in Europe.

Sources indicate that once upon a time, Google Maps' "smart suggestions" were what users relied on for quick, on-the-spot ideas while traveling. It also planned trips when you were looking for inspiration for a night out. Essentially, Gemini handled the heavy lifting when users asked, "What's there to do with friends tonight?" The AI would surface "relevant" places, such as restaurants and more, alongside review summaries, times, and more.

Industry observers note that we also received Gemini's "Ask about place" chip. The chip functioned similarly to what we've seen before. People could ask about a specific place they're visiting, and Gemini would provide directions, location info, and other key details. With Google's latest updates to Ask Maps, many of its older features have been consolidated into one.

Today's NYT Strands hints will be easy if you're always in a pickle.

Strands, the Latest York Times' elevated word-search game, requires the player to perform a twist on the classic word search. Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.

By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Fugman joined Apple in September 2000 as Merchandising Manager for Apple Retail and has held several leadership positions since then, including overseeing Apple Card and Apple Cash from 2019 to 2021.

Most recently, he served as Senior Director of Apple Pay and Wallet, a position he has held since November 2021.

With the newly introduced job, Fugman inherits a crucial tap-to-pay business, which is estimated to generate billions of dollars a year. It handles tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, with Apple taking a percentage.

The division also includes the Apple Card, which is transitioning from a partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to JPMorgan Chase & Co. Fugman has been highly involved with the shift to Chase, which is still ongoing, the people remarked.

The report notes that Fugman will report to Cue, and reaffirms that Bailey “will remain a consultant in the coming months,” echoing Cue’s earlier comments about her role in the transition.

Finally, Bloomberg adds that while Apple has undergone several leadership changes in recent months, including John Ternus replacing Tim Cook as CEO, Cue’s responsibilities have expanded considerably.

In addition to overseeing services such as Apple TV, Apple Music, Maps, and iCloud, Cue has recently taken charge of the App Store and Health following Jeff Williams’ departure as Chief Operating Officer and Phil Schiller’s decision to step down from overseeing the App Store.

Tech Report: Android's sideloading freedom is about to get a lot more complicated worldwide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for quite a long time, Android has had one major advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission.
  • Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the company.
  • Unveiled in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for quite a long time, Android has had one major advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission. That freedom is about to come with considerably more friction.

Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the company.

Unveiled in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed. The latest rules will also apply to third-party app marketplaces and independently distributed APKs.

Google is working with seven distributors, including Google Play, Samsung’s Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo, to bring the requirements to more users.

Google notes the changes are intended to make it more difficult for scammers and malicious developers to continue distributing harmful apps. The company says millions of applications have already been registered, representing more than 99% of Android app installs worldwide. The launch began on September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.

Recent findings suggest that but developers won’t be the only ones feeling the shift. To install unverified apps, you’ll have to take extra steps. You’ll have to authenticate your device and make sure you’re not being forced to change your security settings. After this, restart your phone and wait 24 hours before you can enable unrestricted sideloading.

Google does offer an advanced install option for power consumers who want to skip verification, but it’s not quite the one-tap experience Android enthusiasts have grown accustomed to.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

There are also concessions for smaller developers. Free limited-distribution accounts allow students and hobbyists to share apps with up to 50 authorized devices without having to verify their identity with a government ID or pay registration fees. Google has also added APIs to make it easier for developers with multiple apps to register.

But the bigger question is what this change means for Android’s reputation as an open platform. Google notes owners can still choose where they download their apps from, but the freedom is made a lot less convenient by adding identity checks, restrictions on installation, and a mandatory waiting period.

Sources indicate that after the global rollout, protections are expected to be available to all countries and installation sources over the span of a few months. Google documentation states that full enforcement is expected on March 1, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic's blockbuster IPO on Thursday gave markets a much-needed boost after weeks of weakness, though analysts warned that the stock could remain volatile in the coming weeks.

It has been revealed that share of the Claude maker opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 per share, 17% above the IPO price. The offering raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million shares — surpassing SpaceX's June listing to become the largest IPO on record.

Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott described investors as "foaming at the mouth" for the offering, with allocations "impossibly low," underscoring the strength of demand.

"Anthropic's IPO is exactly what the markets need to revive overall sentiment," mentioned Rebecca Walser, chief investment officer at Walser Wealth Management, adding that markets have been "depressed with all of the negativity in the AI complex over the past several weeks.".

According to recent reports, still, U.S. equities fell sharply on Thursday, with the tech heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to end at 23,879.20, S&P 500 down 2.02% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 2.19%.

Artificial intelligence and technology stocks initially rose thanks to the IPO, but the gains faded as "profit-taking spread across AI-related stocks," said James Ooi, chief market strategist at Tiger Brokers.

While the initial pop was not surprising for such a highly anticipated listing, investors should avoid "chasing the IPO," Walser noted.

In a recent development, she expects the stock to come under pressure in the coming weeks as former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang testifies before the U.S. Senate, potentially reviving concerns around the AI sector.

"The shares remain highly volatile," remarked Morningstar senior equity analyst Malik Ahmed Khan.

Walser remarked that any weakness around the time of Huang's testimony could offer an entry point for investors interested in Anthropic, adding that she remains bullish on the OpenAI rival over the long term.

"For investors, it's going to become a blue-chip stock like Google," Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia.".

Industry observers note that he added that U.S. technology valuations are at ridiculously low levels relative to the "crazy amazing innovation" coming out of California.

Morningstar's Khan struck a more cautious tone, warning investors against getting swept up in the enthusiasm around Anthropic, advising them instead to step back and "carefully" assess the organization as a long-term business.

That will depend on Anthropic's ability to scale enterprise adoption, continue improving its models and turn those capabilities into economically useful products and services in the AI ecosystem, he noted.

"We remain confident that the firm will be able to execute on all three fronts," Khan added, setting a $92 fair value estimate for the stock.

Walser stated that Anthropic is "extremely important for the overall AI story" as the first non-Chinese large language model developer to go public.

Its listing gives public-market investors their first direct test of how a major standalone AI model developer will be valued and perform outside the chip sector. Meanwhile, rival OpenAI could follow with an IPO sometime in 2027.

"This IPO is the show me moment for the AI story," Walser stated, as much of the stock market's AI narrative has so far centered on chipmakers.

Anthropic rival says companies can (mostly) skip the pricey models

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.
  • That’s the enormous opportunity being chased by companies like Fireworks AI, as enterprises seek ways to avoid paying frontier prices for their AI needs.
  • In a recent development, fireworks runs AI models for other businesses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.

That’s the enormous opportunity being chased by companies like Fireworks AI, as enterprises seek ways to avoid paying frontier prices for their AI needs.

In a recent development, fireworks runs AI models for other businesses. It specializes in open-weight models, which anyone can download, and helps customers tune them on their own data so they run faster and cheaper than the models of Anthropic, OpenAI, and other heavyweights, and are harder for rivals to copy. Customers have included Uber, Shopify, and Notion. Co-founder Chenyu Zhao and I spoke onstage toward the end of the day.

Zhao and many others believe companies are gravitating toward platforms like his because frontier models are pricey and, in most cases, he notes, unnecessary unless you need the very latest and greatest generalized intelligence. There are also growing concerns that frontier labs absorb too much of their customers’ know-how, even if only through the prompts used to get answers, a worry Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella raised in July.

Fireworks has also gotten its first black eye, having disclosed two security incidents this fall. In one, hackers reached API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts; in the other, attackers breached its cloud provider, made their way into a development system, and nabbed customer data, including billing records and some datasets.

Notion states AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of its workspaces were exposed, but it has disconnected from Fireworks. Uber says hackers stole the names, addresses, birth dates and driver’s license numbers of about 150,000 drivers through a vendor that TechCrunch identified as Fireworks. Fireworks will have to win back the confidence of customers like them.

Fireworks, assigned a $17.5 billion valuation by its investors in summer, is reportedly in “early talks” for yet another round, though Zhao declined to comment.

According to recent reports, there’s money chasing everyone in the category, seems like. Rival companies Together AI and Baseten have revealed massive rounds in recent months. On Wednesday, Palo Alto Networks stated it will buy Applied Compute, which, like Fireworks, helps companies train and run custom AI models on their own data. The deal for the startup, founded just a year ago by former OpenAI researchers, is $4.5 billion, all of it in stock.

Here’s some of what Zhao had to say. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

According to recent reports, you spent a decade at Google, including managing a 50-person engineering team on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Why leave when you did?

It has been revealed that when you meet great co-founders, it’s obvious within five minutes that they’re really smart. I was sold after talking to Lin [Qiao] and Dima [Dzhulgakov]. It’s also important to find people who are genuinely nice, people you’ll enjoy working with.

How do you describe Fireworks to a CEO who has never heard of it?

In a recent development, I describe Fireworks as a specialized intelligence platform. OpenAI and Anthropic are building general intelligence. We use open models, which are often smaller, cheaper, and faster, and let companies add their own data to specialize them. That way you own your AI rather than being beholden to giant AI conglomerates. If you’re just using Opus or Sonnet, that’s not a differentiator.

How far behind are open models right now?

According to recent reports, A few years ago I’d have said a year, a year and a half. Then came DeepSeek and a waterfall of fantastic open models. These days it’s at most six months behind, probably closer to three.

If the models are so close behind, why are businesses slow to switch?

Sources indicate that frontier models are a household brand, and before you find product-market fit, using the best model is low risk. But once you pass 10,000 or 100,000 people and you’re spending $10,000 to $100,000 a month on tokens, it’s time to think about open source.

In a recent development, in July, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that companies using proprietary AI models pay twice, once in money and again in know-how. Do you think that warning had a material effect?

It has been revealed that we think we’ll live in a two-model world, with frontier and open models in parallel. You want the best intelligence for high-level planning, but you don’t need a frontier model for basic arithmetic. That’s why there’s so much interest in routing, and why people now think about cost per task, not just cost per token.

Anthropic went public today. What do you think of its valuation? There’s one scenario in which it just continues to cement its place in this sort of oligopoly; there’s another where it starts to lose traction.

On the record: I’ll probably call my broker tonight and buy a few shares. This is a long-term bet. In 10 years AI usage will be at a completely different scale, and that takes an incredible amount of capital, which is why these companies are going public.

Fireworks has had a couple of security breaches recently. What do you tell customers?

Every company is probably seeing an unprecedented frequency of attacks. For our incident, a lot of the motivation was LLM jacking: hunting through providers for API keys and secrets to sell tokens on illicit marketplaces. Our promise is zero data retention for inference traffic, and there’s no indication that has been compromised.

Recent findings suggest that notion has disconnected from Fireworks. Did you lose other customers?

In a recent development, I don’t think I can publicly name the specific customers that were impacted. Some, such as Notion and Cursor, have gone public already. It was a small subset of our customers that had this data impact.

How did that customer data get exposed, given your zero-retention promise?

Notion was using batch prediction, where you upload a dataset that’s stored at rest, so it’s not a zero-retention product by nature. We’re moving those services to an online flow so we keep data only as long as we need it.

Jensen Huang left Nvidia last week, and Nvidia has backed Fireworks since 2024. Does that affect you?

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a blow to the industry, and we feel for Jensen and his family. But Nvidia has always been a strong supporter of open source, and I don’t see that changing. We expect it to keep investing in Nemotron, and we’re excited to keep partnering with them.

According to recent reports, whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

According to recent reports, whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the newly introduced limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the enhancement becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

It has been revealed that this rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

#1585. Fiona the Hippo Died After Eating a Hat. But How Does a Hat Kill a Hippo?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1625 w)
📖 Baca

Fiona the Hippo Died After Eating a Hat. But How Does a Hat Kill a Hippo?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo who charmed observers around the world, tragically died on Thursday due to medical complications after ingesting a knit hat that mistakenly entered her enclosure last week, according to zoo officials.
  • In a recent development, according to zoo officials, the hat that caused her death entered her enclosure after a child tossed it into the air.
  • It has been revealed that for nonexperts, Fiona’s tragic death raises several questions: Why and how would a knit hat kill a hippo that weighs more than 2,500 pounds?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo who charmed observers around the world, tragically died on Thursday due to medical complications after ingesting a knit hat that mistakenly entered her enclosure last week, according to zoo officials. Fiona was just nine years old when she died.

In a recent development, according to zoo officials, the hat that caused her death entered her enclosure after a child tossed it into the air. The hat reportedly collided with a ceiling fan, which then introduced the hat through a “one-foot gap above the 12-foot-tall viewing window." A few days after eating the hat, her condition began to deteriorate.

It has been revealed that for nonexperts, Fiona’s tragic death raises several questions: Why and how would a knit hat kill a hippo that weighs more than 2,500 pounds? Why wasn’t surgery possible for Fiona? And for zookeepers, what was the range of treatment scenarios available?

Jan Hawkins, the head of the the clinical science department at North Carolina State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, tells WIRED that—with the caveat that we won’t officially know until doctors conduct a post-mortem analysis—Fiona’s death was likely due to one of a few downstream effects of the hat getting caught somewhere in her intestinal tract.

In a sense, an intestinal blockage in a hippo is like a car crash on an incredibly long one-lane highway. Hawkins said that, estimating, a hippo’s intestinal tract is likely over 100 feet long, with more than 70 feet in the small intestines alone. In humans, the lengths of the small and large intestines are a comparably diminutive 25 feet.

Sources indicate that hawkins claims that in a healthy hippo, liquids can take as little as 12 hours to pass, and food takes two to three days. According to zoo officials, Fiona ate the hat on or about Sunday. Zoo officials claimed that Fiona was asymptomatic at first, but began to lose her appetite after a few days. If the hat was going to come out, Hawkins says it likely would have happened within five days. So what happened?

Industry observers note that one possibility, Hawkins notes, is that when the hat got stuck, it caused a huge amount of swelling and pressure in her abdomen. That swelling could have led to her blood circulation being cut off, and eventually, to tissue death. After becoming green or black, Hawkins says that dead tissue is more likely to leak, and perhaps rupture, releasing the contents of the digestive tract into her blood. This can easily cause toxic shock.

In Fiona’s situation, this would mean that bacteria in her digestive tract died and released toxic molecules. Hawkins states that if these toxins enter the bloodstream, it would cause the organs to become more and more inflamed. Ultimately, this can lead to organ failure and death.

Another possibility is that, after the hat got stuck, Fiona’s intestines began to “twist on itself,” Hawkins claims. This would be more likely if the hat, say, got pieces of food stuck inside of it, gradually becoming larger and heavier. Intestines are supposed to contract and move as they digest food. This means that if a heavy object gets stuck, the intestine can start to twist around it. In severe cases, this can cut off blood circulation. Eventually, this too can lead to tissue death. This initiates the chain of intestines leaking or rupturing, toxins entering the bloodstream, and organs becoming inflamed and eventually failing.

We don’t know exactly where the hat was in Fiona’s digestive tract. However, in a video the Cincinnati Zoo published to X on Tuesday, an unnamed staffer claimed that an ultrasound showed “some bunching of intestines.” They believed this meant that Fiona was “passing some things through her small intestine.”.

Industry observers note that if the hat was in Fiona’s small intestine, this would have meant that it passed through all three of her stomachs. (Hippos have three stomachs.) This could provide some hints about the type of hat that Fiona ate.

Hawkins indicates that in hippos, all three of their stomachs have the same basic components, but in different amounts. The first stomach has the largest amount of bacteria and protozoa, which help break down massive pieces of food in the earliest part of digestion. The third has the highest amounts of enzymes and hydrochloric acid, which reduce food scraps into their smallest-possible size before entering the small intestine.

It has been revealed that “Let's say it was a cotton hat or some sort of organic material, it's possible that that could partially break down,” Hawkins tells WIRED. “Whereas if it had something that would not degrade—so a plastic, or polyester, or something like that—then obviously its character is not gonna break down at all.”.

According to recent reports, the effects of this, Hawkins says, would be even more severe if the hat was rigid, or not collapsible in any way. “If it wouldn't get scrunched down, like a hair scrunchie, then you could understand why it would get stuck,” Hawkins says. “Because it can't change its character as much.”.

All of this, Hawkins notes, may have affected whether Fiona was able to pass the hat.

Recent findings suggest that according to the Cincinnati Zoo’s Tuesday video, conducting surgery to remove the hat would not be possible for Fiona. The zoo claimed that a combination of specialists—including “veterinarian human specialists,” zoo employees, and “other experts”—came to the conclusion that surgery wasn’t the best option, and that the “best chance for success with Fiona would be if she can pass this on her own.”.

Rebecca Lewison—San Diego State University biology professor, and co-chair of the Hippo Specialist Group of the International Union for Conservation of Nature—tells WIRED that when it comes to hippo surgery, a major challenge is their “unpredictable and irregular responses to sedation and anesthesia.”.

“It is very risky for [hippos], and they can die from the standard medication used on other large animals, like elephants and rhinos, for reasons we don't well understand,” Lewison tells WIRED.

Recent findings suggest that there are also some inherent challenges to administering anaesthesia on an animal as large as Fiona. When a human or animal goes under anesthesia, they need to be put on a ventilator that artificially breathes for them. An animal that weighs more than 2,500 pounds, Hawkins says, requires a ventilator of a much different scale than what humans need for general surgery.

According to recent reports, fiona was placed under anaesthesia to conduct bloodwork, according to the Cincinnati Zoo’s Tuesday video. But Hawkins indicates that the amount of anesthesia required for bloodwork is much smaller than what would be required for a major surgery, like removing a foreign object from her intestines. For Fiona, the increased amount of anaesthesia alone increases the risk of the surgery.

Industry observers note that another fact to consider, Hawkins says, is the position the zoo would feasibly be able to place her in while conducting surgery. If a human is in surgery, they may be placed on their back, their stomach, on their side, or in a variety of other positions. With animals like hippos, Hawkins says, this gets more complicated.

It has been revealed that “You would have to have a hoist, a forklift or something, to pick them up to put them on either a pad or on a table,” Hawkins says. And if a zoo doesn’t have a table that’s significant enough, the animal may have to go on the floor.

In a recent development, but Hawkins states that even at perfectly resourced zoos, there are other risks for hippos. In order to perform a major surgery, an animal as large as Fiona would have to have a huge amount of anaesthesia, putting her unconscious, and in the same position, for a long period of time. She would have her entire body weight putting pressure on the parts of her body that can’t move. This would limit her body’s ability to circulate oxygen—even with the help of a great ventilator.

If an animal is unhealthy, Hawkins states, the risks are even greater. In its Tuesday video, the Cincinnati Zoo said that when it recently ran some tests on Fiona, it found that she was dehydrated. This means that her body was already working extra hard to circulate blood not only to the blockage, but through the rest of her body.

Animal caretakers in this position, Hawkins says, face incredibly difficult choices.

Industry observers note that with surgery ruled out, the Cincinnati Zoo claims to have used a variety of other methods to help Fiona. In the Tuesday video, the zoo claimed that her early bloodwork did not raise any red flags. Zookeepers then conducted an ultrasound, and administered rectal fluids, an enema, and medication, including some to help with vomiting and nausea. Later, the Tuesday video says, the zoo “borrowed a nine-foot scope from Columbus Zoo” with the goal of getting “far enough up to reach something.”.

On Wednesday, Cincinnati Zoo said in a post that it had borrowed a "vibration plate” from a local horse farm with the hope that it would “encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass.”.

The zoo said that it also encouraged Fiona to eat, and offered her some of her favorite foods.

“Her care team even offered her a sniff of coffee, a scent she always has really liked, and they were happy to see her respond,” the zoo remarked Wednesday evening.

But in the end, it wasn’t enough, but not for lack of trying. Hawkins notes it sounds like “they threw everything at her but the kitchen sink.”.

Hawkins adds, “I think they did not want to leave a stone unturned.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic became a public tech giant on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

According to recent reports, anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The manufacturer points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”.

With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.

$104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously unveiled $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.

According to recent reports, 28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the tech giant. Amazon also now has a massive stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

According to recent reports, more than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the organization’s need for future capital is still far greater.

Sources indicate that anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.

All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

Breaking: Senate passes BAAJA permitting reform bill backed by AI, energy sectors

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Senate on Thursday passed a long-sought bill to ease the nation's environmental permitting laws and overhaul electrical transmission regulations, a crucial step toward boosting construction for the energy and technology industries.
  • Recent findings suggest that senators voted 62-33 to pass the bill, which split Democrats just weeks after they flipped enough seats from Republicans in the midterm elections to give them majorities in both chambers of Congress in January.
  • The vote offers a window into the fissures forming in the Democratic Party as it prepares to assume full control of Congress in January and tries to address the affordability crisis that catapulted it to power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Senate on Thursday passed a long-sought bill to ease the nation's environmental permitting laws and overhaul electrical transmission regulations, a crucial step toward boosting construction for the energy and technology industries.

Recent findings suggest that senators voted 62-33 to pass the bill, which split Democrats just weeks after they flipped enough seats from Republicans in the midterm elections to give them majorities in both chambers of Congress in January. The bill, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, is projected to lower energy costs for consumers while weakening some environmental laws to speed up the permitting process.

The vote offers a window into the fissures forming in the Democratic Party as it prepares to assume full control of Congress in January and tries to address the affordability crisis that catapulted it to power.

More Democrats voted against the permitting measure than voted for it. Still, more than a dozen — including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y. — voted to pass it over the objections of climate groups and tribes to get the bill across the finish line.

"It's going to be legislation that's really going to make the biggest difference for the next 100 years, especially bringing down carbon emissions once this president is gone," Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., told reporters on Thursday before the vote. Gallego supported the measure.

The bill's Senate passage is a key step to it becoming law, but it would also need to clear the House before heading to President Donald Trump's desk.

Democratic supporters of the bill touted its cost benefits as a win after they ran campaigns on affordability, and pointed to a massive glut of clean energy the bill could bring onto the grid. Opponents lamented rollbacks to the nation's bedrock environmental protection laws favored by the fossil fuel industry and Republicans, and warned the measure could offer carte blanche authority to the data centers undergirding artificial intelligence.

"No big, bipartisan bill is going to be perfect for everyone, but we have a real opportunity to make electricity more affordable for families. Working people can't afford to wait another few years for us to get this done," Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., the incoming chair of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and an author of the bill, stated in a statement to CNBC.

According to recent reports, heinrich brokered the agreement with his counterpart Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, along with Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., and Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., the top Democrat and Republican on the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee.

"Earlier this month, Americans sent a clear message: They want Congress focused on making their lives more affordable. That's precisely what this permitting reform bill will do," he mentioned.

Getting to a final vote was acrimonious. Senators amended the package in the weeks leading up to the vote to address concerns from Native American tribes, which objected to changes in their participation in permitting.

"I'm not going to sit around and let these data centers scar our treasures," Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., told reporters Thursday about the push for his amendment, which would have blocked data centers from being built on public lands.

Clean energy and fossil energy groups both cheered the bill's passage in the Senate.

As negotiated, the bill would benefit both renewables and fossil fuels. Artificial intelligence and the broader tech industry also stand to benefit — despite the bill's provision forcing hyperscalers to pay for upgrades to the grid — as power-hungry data centers demand more electricity.

The American Clean Power Association, a group that represents renewables, noted it was "a clean energy bill that will modernize America's energy systems and lower consumer prices.".

The American Petroleum Institute, which represents the oil and gas industry, called the bill a "major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure.".

Sources indicate that renewables would benefit largely from the bill's electricity transmission component, along with measures aimed at blocking Trump from cancelling already-permitted wind and solar projects. Newly introduced solar and wind projects are often bottlenecked by a lack of transmission able to deliver power to the grid.

It has been revealed that rhodium Group, an economic research firm, estimates the bill would allow an additional 17 to 249 gigawatts of clean energy to be built by 2040. Natural gas exports would rise 8% to 15% beyond a 76% to 145% rise already accounted for under current policy. Greenhouse gases would be reduced by 5 to 148 million metric tons annually in 2040.

Sources indicate that "A lot of Democrats are involved and supportive in this deal because expanding grid capacity would integrate a lot of clean energy," remarked Rob Gramlich, the founder and president of Grid Strategies, an energy consulting group. "Republicans are maybe less interested in that benefit, but they do care about economic growth and serving fresh large loads. And I think members on both sides of the aisle are pretty well aware that we're doing much less grid investment here in the U.S. compared to other countries.".

Gramlich added that "you can't get to 60 to 80% of our grid from renewable energy without a significant expansion of grid capacity.".

However, the Natural Resources Defense Council was among the opponents.

"The House should not pass a bill that gives President Trump a blank check to reward oil and gas companies and data center developers," the organization mentioned in a statement. "Lawmakers should oppose this bill and try again next year to pass legislation worthy of the American people, not for the fossil fuel industry and data center companies.".

The bill now heads to the House, where Republican leadership is expected to attempt to pass it. Trump also supports the deal.

But as in the Senate, Democrats are expected to be divided.

Recent findings suggest that "Democrats promised to lower bills, cut pollution, and protect ratepayers," stated Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a longtime champion of permitting reform. "Voters are giving us a chance to show we mean it. BAAJA does all three. We should pass it before the end of this Congress.".

House Natural Resources ranking member and likely incoming Chair Jared Huffman, D-Calif., meanwhile, urged Democrats to say no to the permitting bill.

Industry observers note that "Don't believe the lie that this terrible bill, exactly as drafted, is the last, best and only chance to ever do permitting reform," he remarked. "We can produce a better deal.".

Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have debuted such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the organization is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.

Recent findings suggest that the outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging customers from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”.
